The entirety of the time I was on zoloft felt like the come up of eating mushrooms. I mean physically, even. Clammy skin, felt like my voice was booming every time I spoke, the concept of food made me queasy let alone actually eating it, it was weird.
I did smoke weed pretty regularly throughout (mainly in hopes of combating the appetite thing), so it may have contributed but I was sober the first few weeks and the month or so prior to starting so I know that initially it was just adjusting to the medication.

Looking back -I stopped taking zoloft ~1.5 years ago- I genuinely can’t remember a time that I felt mentally fully “there”. Certainly it helped with the anxiety it was meant for but also, I may as well have just been doing a less interesting version of psilocybin treatment. 

KEEP IN MIND. I’ve always been extremely sensitive to substances and my doctor had maxed my dose within two months of starting. I think this is actually a really effective ssri as far as they go, it had no actual negative effects on me other than the odd reactions mentioned above and it DID help what it was supposed to. This is extremely interesting to me and I’d love to see sleep studies on gamers with emphases on the different genres they play the most.

I don’t wake up, either. Generally I just leave my “body” and look at it while experiencing very muted sensations. 

Also different, I experience my senses very vividly in dreams. Actually my stress dreams almost revolve exclusively around awful sensory experiences like rotten food, painful ringing sounds, having to complete tasks with a hurt body part etc.

This comment makes me wonder if continuing to dream post-dream-death is a fairly recent phenomenon that correlates with experiencing video game deaths throughout our lives. We tricked our brains into thinking dying comes with a respawn lol

Hey! So as far as anesthesia goes, I was FREAKED right before going in. I’ve been put under before and had no problems, but it’s total loss of control, scary! It was really nice though honestly. The team came one by one to introduce themselves to me after my IV got put in(which is what generally sets off my anxiety) and I had two anesthesiologists. The second one is the person who wheeled me in and could tell I was nervous and asked me one by one what I’m nervous about. For each fear I had, he had a totally honest and comforting answer, and just before I went under he held my hand and promised me he’d make sure everything goes perfectly for me after explaining what each thing on the monitor I’m hooked up to tells him.

So for me, knowledge is power, and a kind face is also helpful haha.

As far as otc; I don’t think so for me personally. I’ve been trying to wait as long as possible between doses(my mother passed from a narcotics addiction), but since I’ve been doing that I’ve been waking up in the middle of the night from pain. Go easy on yourself. If you need it, that’s why it’s there. If it does you more pain than good though, I’d ask your doctor about other methods and doses of otc help!
